definitions.explanation: Lacking anything special or outstanding; neither particularly good nor bad. Can describe people, lives, abilities, or things. Sometimes carries a slightly negative nuance of being dull or unexceptional.

examples.japanese: {平凡|へいぼん}な{毎日|まいにち}を{送|おく}る。
{彼|かれ}は{平凡|へいぼん}なサラリーマンだ。
examples.english: He is an ordinary office worker.

examples.japanese: {平凡|へいぼん}な{幸|しあわ}せこそが{一番|いちばん}{大切|たいせつ}だと{気|き}づいた。
examples.english: I realized that ordinary happiness is the most important thing.

notes:
A な-adjective from {平凡|へいぼん}, a compound of {平|へい} (flat, ordinary) and {凡|ぼん} (ordinary, mediocre). The word can be neutral (simply meaning ordinary) or slightly negative (implying dullness or mediocrity), depending on context.

USAGE:
When used about oneself, it often conveys humility. When used about others or things, it can imply they are unremarkable or disappointing. However, in expressions like {平凡|へいぼん}な{幸|しあわ}せ (ordinary happiness), it takes on a positive nuance of appreciating the simple things in life.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {平凡|へいぼん}な{人生|じんせい} — an ordinary life
- {平凡|へいぼん}な{日常|にちじょう} — everyday ordinariness
- {非凡|ひぼん} — extraordinary (antonym, using the same {凡|ぼん})

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {普通|ふつう} — normal, ordinary (more neutral, everyday word)
- {地味|じみ} — plain, understated (focuses on appearance)
- {凡庸|ぼんよう} — mediocre (more literary, more negative)
